maria: quick share — ran a few nsys + perfetto passes on prod-sim (kv-heavy), attaching quick numbers and a small timeline link: https://perf.redwood/traces/1769001234 :point_down:

maria: TL;DR: full nsys trace shows ~18% tail-latency inflation on 512-token workloads; lightweight sampling mode (perfetto CPU-only sampling) shows ~2.5% overhead but misses some CUDA kernel sequencing info.

maria: main hotspots identified from full trace: repeated small memcpy+kernel launch around KV eviction, softmax kernel in attention for long history, and a 3x spike in rendezvous synchronization on some hosts.

lee: thanks — can you paste the exact nsys command you ran? want to reproduce locally.

maria: ran: ```nsys profile --output=run-1769001234 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx``` then exported perfetto timeline. also tried `nsys profile --sample=cpu` which lowered overhead but missed CUDA launch timelines.

darren: 18% matches my earlier regression run when we had the kernel-switch heuristic flipped on. is this with the new kernel selector (v2) enabled?

maria: yes v2 kernel selector + dynamic-batching=on. suspect selector is bouncing between int8-optimized kernel and fp16 fallback for some sequence lengths because KV cache padding is weird.

vivian: interesting — padding/prefill of kv cache can change sequence lengths and trigger different kernel paths. did you capture per-op op_name and chosen kernel in trace?

maria: full nsys export includes kernel names and launch attributes. sample of kernel lines: ```attention_softmax_fwd_fp16_kernel, 1.2ms; kv_read_copy_kernel, 0.42ms; kv_swap_out_kernel, 0.9ms```

lee: for safe-prod profiling we should avoid full nsys continuous. proposal: low-touch sampling profile that collects a short full trace (nsys) only occasionally and otherwise uses perfetto sampling plus NVTX markers to reconstruct higher-level flow.

darren: agree. suggested guardrails:
- only sample on <5% of requests per instance
- limit to 1 full nsys capture per GPU per 6h
- disable on instances with current p95 > SLA_threshold
- require ops approval for Dedicated customers

maria: from experiments: 1 full nsys capture for 30s on an idle host was ~12% cost in that window; continuous full tracing was killing tail p99. Perfetto sampling at 1000Hz CPU-only was ~2.5% and gave good event timing for thread-level but no CUDA kernel internals.

vivian: could we stitch together by doing NVTX + lightweight timestamped kernel counters? e.g., enable `cupti_activity` counters (low-overhead) + perfetto sampling and then correlate via NVTX spans.

lee: yes — approach:
1) add NVTX spans around batching boundary, kv read/write, and kernel selection decision points.
2) perfetto CPU sampling + CUPTI lightweight activities (kernels only) by default.
3) rotate 1 GPU per host to run a 20–30s nsys capture every 4h to get full CUDA timeline for a subset of traces.

maria: any objections to the rotate+sample cadence? want to write a rollout plan for eng-runtime.

darren: one more constraint — don't run nsys on hosts that are currently under high burst load (CPU or GPU util > 70%). infra-bot can help gate.

infra-bot: note: I can publish a host label `trace-eligible` and maintain a short TTL. can also annotate if p95 exceeded in last 5m. use `/infra trace-eligible add <host>` to opt-in.

vivian: nice. also add opt-out for tenants where we must never sample (Dedicated with strict SLAs).

lee: for kernel-selector debugging we should add histograms of chosen kernel id by seq_len bucket and batch size. that will let us see selector flip churn. keep those histos at low cardinality (5 bins) to avoid metric cost.

maria: I'll collect a quick CSV from the trace with columns: timestamp, nvtx_span, kernel_name, seq_len, batch_size, chosen_kernel_id, kv_cache_hit. sample attached gist: https://gist.redwood/trace-csv-1769001234

darren: for rollout steps (proposal):
- stage: internal dev hosts, 2 days capture, verify no p99 regressions
- stage: prod-sim which we already used (today)
- canary: 5% of inference fleet for 24h with perfetto+cup­ti only
- ramp: enable 1 GPU rotate nsys 20s/4h for 10% of fleet for 7d
- full: enable low-touch sampling everywhere with infra gate and opt-outs

maria: will draft a runbook with guardrails (max captures/day per GPU, CPU/GPU util threshold, tenant opt-out list, emergency off switch). putting a short checklist here:
- monitor p95 and p99 during cadence (alert if +5% over baseline)
- auto-disable captures when node_util > 70%
- avoid sampling during nightly batch jobs
- store full traces to secure bucket with retention 30d

vivian: on storage: redact any customer prompt content before upload — strip request payloads or store only spans and kernel metadata.

lee: one more thought — we can use tiny inference load generators to reproduce the kernel churn locally once we have a candidate trace. makes debugging faster than waiting for a rotation sample.

maria: action items:
- maria: draft runbook + NVTX placement PR (today)
- lee: add kernel-id histograms to metrics pipeline (this week)
- darren: infra gating work + `trace-eligible` label (this week)
- vivian: privacy redaction checklist + storage policy (this week)

darren: thanks — if folks agree I'll schedule the canary next Tue 09:00 UTC.

vivian: +1

lee: +1

maria: +1, will open the PRs and link them here.```
